concerns.text: The plan identifies a critical gap: no verified source exists for the target variable (experimental gas permeability). The proposed 'Fallback' strategy to 'generate a simulated permeability target based on geometric descriptors' creates a circular validation. If the target is derived from the same geometric descriptors (surface area, pore volume) that the GNN or baselines use as inputs (or learn from the graph structure), the model is mathematically guaranteed to correlate with the target. This renders the RMSE and Pearson r metrics trivial and non-empirical, failing to validate the hypothesis that joint encoding improves prediction of *real* physical phenomena.

The ablation study (FR-006) and sensitivity analysis (FR-007) rely on the 'cross_contact' edges. If the target variable is simulated based on geometric proxies (as proposed in the fallback), the 'cross_contact' edges (which are also geometric distance-based) will likely be the primary driver of the simulated target. The resulting 'performance delta' (SC-003) will be a tautological confirmation of the simulation logic rather than an empirical test of the GNN's ability to capture non-covalent interactions in real permeability data.

The plan proposes using a 'simulated' target to test 'pipeline mechanics' while flagging the lack of real validation. However, the Success Criteria (SC-001 to SC-006) and User Stories (US-2, US-3) are framed as if they are measuring scientific utility (e.g., 'determine if joint encoding improves permeability prediction accuracy'). Running a regression model on a synthetic target derived from the input features does not answer the research question regarding molecular permeability; it only answers 'does the model fit the synthetic function I wrote.' The methodology is mismatched to the claimed scientific goal.
